verdict.rationale: Smithery's build docs describe publishing your own MCP server. You can publish by URL, ship local stdio servers as MCPB bundles, supply a static server card when scanning fails, and get a dedicated server page for discovery and installation. The CLI offers registry search and add. However, the October 31, 2026 shutdown removed the docs tree and stopped Smithery accounts and API keys, so it is unclear whether new servers can still be published, even though the registry remains public. Missing for 10: confirmation that publishing still works after the shutdown, a documented post-shutdown publishing flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration of publishing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: If you’ve already deployed an MCP server elsewhere, you can publish it directly on Smithery via the URL method.
Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Smithery will remain as a public (non-proxied) MCP registry.
